message: The acknowledgement watermark is the goal entity's updatedAt, which any write to the goal bumps - including the staff member's own edits in the NS calculator. After a user views the card, opens the wizard and saves a field, the card returns on the dashboard saying "Your goal changed since you last looked", which is false.

The GqlMockedProvider UserOption mock is not parameterized by the `key` variable, so it returns the same fixture ({key:"user_type_verified", value:"true"}) for both ConfirmUserGroupModal's check and NewStaffGoalReadyCard's own `new_staff_goal_acknowledged_goal-1` lookup. The test only passes because "true" happens to parse as an invalid Date (NaN), so it coincidentally looks unacknowledged rather than because the mock actually answers the right key.
No test covers a GraphQL error response for NewStaffGoalReady or UserOption, so a regression that leaves the card stuck loading/crashing on an Apollo error would go undetected.

The card forks the eligibility gate every other nsGoalCalculator entry point uses: it checks only DISABLE_NS_GOAL_CALCULATOR and inNsGoalCalcIneligibleGroup, omitting reportsDisabled and the userType check. The card and its link can therefore appear for users the nav hides the tool from, and for users the page itself answers with LimitedAccess.

SentGoalCard does `if (loading || ...) return null` on useUserOptionQuery, whose loading flag goes true again on every refetch under the app-wide cache-and-network + notifyOnNetworkStatusChange policy. This is the documented refetch-flash bug: an already-visible, undismissed card will vanish and reappear on refocus/cache invalidation, not just on first load.

acknowledge() has no error handling on updateUserOption, and no test exercises a rejected mutation; because dismissed is set to true unconditionally before the request resolves, a failed save leaves the card permanently hidden for that session with nothing asserting or fixing that behavior.

The acknowledgement timestamp is parsed with `new Date(string)` instead of Luxon, so a partially parseable non-ISO value (e.g. "2026" or "Sep 2026") reads as a valid acknowledgement in the past and silently flips the card to the "Your MPD goal was updated" copy. The repo convention is `DateTime.fromISO(...).isValid`, because `new Date(arbitraryString)` parsing is implementation-defined per spec.

`if (loading) return null` blanks the card on every refetch of the UserOption query, not just the first load, because the client sets `fetchPolicy: cache-and-network` with `notifyOnNetworkStatusChange: true` — so `loading` goes true again on each remount while cached `data` is already present. That reintroduces exactly the card flash the comment two lines above says this code exists to avoid.

`acknowledge()` sets `dismissed` to true and fires `updateUserOption` without awaiting or catching it, so a failed write produces an unhandled promise rejection and leaves the card hidden for the rest of the session while nothing was persisted — it silently returns on the next page load. The optimistic response is never rolled back into visible state.

New key "Your goal changed since you last looked..." is inserted after "Your MPD goal was updated" instead of before "Your MPD goal is ready", which is where crowdin/sort-translations.js (a.localeCompare(b)) would place it.

StaffMemberDrawer.tsx now renders the Employment Type row via transformAssignmentCategoryGroup(assignmentCategoryGroup, t) instead of the hardcoded pendingField placeholder, but StaffMemberDrawer.test.tsx has no assertion on this row for either a populated or null assignmentCategoryGroup. A regression that reverts this line to pendingField would not be caught by any test.

MpdAssignmentCategoryGroupEnum is mapped to display labels in two places: the new transformAssignmentCategoryGroup helper and the filter panel MenuItem children. The repo rule is one enum value maps to one label, so the dropdown and the row/drawer can drift apart on the next copy change.

transformAssignmentCategoryGroup already returns early for null/undefined, so the trailing default branch is unreachable for every value the type allows. It converts a future schema enum member from a compile error into a silent em dash in the UI.
dismissalDetail: the default branch is a deliberate runtime fallback for server enum values the client doesn't know yet; the unreachable-branch defect is gone (the early null return was removed) and helpers.test.ts covers the unknown-value path

message: The test is named "omits assignmentCategoryGroup" but it asserts the variable is sent as an explicit null, so it does not actually prove the argument is omitted.

Test is named 'omits assignmentCategoryGroup until an employment type is chosen' but the assertion checks that the variable is sent with value null, not that the key is omitted from the operation — the name and the behavior it verifies do not match.
The JSDoc comment on transformAssignmentCategoryGroup only restates the function name/signature and adds no non-obvious why, which this repo has repeatedly asked reviewers to trim.

The repo keeps localized enum-label helpers as getLocalizedX in src/lib/functions; this one is named transformAssignmentCategoryGroup and lives in a feature helpers file. Harmless today because the enum is used only here, but it makes the helper hard to find if a second feature needs the same label.

pendingField is documented as "Stands in for fields managedStaff cannot supply yet", but it is now also the placeholder for a field the API does supply as null. Grepping pendingField no longer tells you which fields are still unimplemented.

The MpdGoalAdmin gotcha note still says an empty cohort list means no cohorts exist at all, not that this user has none, and that the context auto-selects the first cohort whenever the list is non-empty. This PR makes coordinators see a role-filtered list (trainingSize > 0), so a coordinator can now get an empty list while cohorts do exist team-wide — the doc no longer matches the code it describes.

This adds a second empty state for the same situation the existing No Training Selected state (PR #2013) was built for, and they act differently: the new one hides the Training selector, the old one keeps it disabled. For coordinators the old branch can no longer be reached, so its comment is now stale, and admins with zero cohorts still get the old copy and layout.
noVisibleCohorts explicitly guards on !cohortsLoading and !cohortsError so the empty-state message does not flash during load or replace a real error, but no test in the diff exercises either guard.
Added inline comment restates what the ternary already shows (replacing CohortBar/ActiveGoalsContent with NullStateBox) rather than explaining a non-obvious why beyond the one useful clause.

The role check waits on userLoading but ignores a GetUser error. If that query fails, isGoalsAdmin comes back false, so an admin gets the coordinator-filtered list and may see a misleading message that cohorts do not include staff in their ministry.

The cohorts memo now filters non-admins to trainingSize > 0, but no test covers a coordinator whose selected cohort disappears from the filtered list after a re-render (e.g. attendees reassigned away mid-session), which is the scenario the useEffect's stale-selection fallback exists for.

Gating the cohort list on GetUser `loading` means the list is emptied and the page shows the loading state on every mount (and any GetUser refetch) even when the user is already cached, because the watchQuery default is cache-and-network with notifyOnNetworkStatusChange. The role is already known from cache at that point, so this adds a network round trip of blank page for no reason.

The Monthly Gross Salary warning marker is rendered with focusable=false inside a CardActionArea that already has an explicit aria-label, so keyboard and screen-reader users tabbing through the report get no indication a staff member has this warning — only sighted mouse users who hover the red icon see it.

healthStatusLabel re-maps MpdHealthStatusEnum to the same four labels as the existing healthLabel in helpers.ts, differing only in case. That breaks the repo rule of one label per enum value: the two copies of the text can drift apart and add a second set of translation keys.

The legend hardcodes the fiscal-quarter month ranges as translated strings, although this same PR adds getQuarterMonthRange to helpers.ts to compute them. There are now two definitions of the fiscal calendar that can disagree.
